answer: Summit-Seeded Identity Sampling: each epoch, a public verifiable random function draws a small random subset of an agent's registered actions for audit against hidden ground-truth checks. An attacker cannot precompute which actions will be sampled, so every fake identity must pay full honest-behavior cost across all actions. Evasion requires maintaining a sable-rare fraction of compliant behavior or risking detection. The per-identity cost scales with action volume, making mass sybils economically unviable while a genuine oasis of sparse agents stays cheap.
